title: Members list sends every pending invite's secret token to the browser
why: The Members page looks right: one member, one pending invite. The response behind it isn't. It carries the token that accepts the invite, and the page only ever uses it as a React key.
finding: `GET /api/orgs/qa-exploration-workspace/members` returned 200 with `invites[0].token` in the body. `MembersPage` reads `s.token` only as a list key; invite links come from the `link` field of `POST /invites`.
actual: GET /api/orgs/qa-exploration-workspace/members returns HTTP 200 with an application/json body containing `invites:[{ "token":"Tq7Xk2Vb9MwR4nLz8PcYd3HsGf6JaE1u", ... }]` — the raw invite token is sent to the browser. The client page only uses that token as a React list key and never for any legitimate client-facing purpose.
expected: The members listing response should not expose invite tokens to the browser. The client needs only the invite's display fields (email, role, status, invitedAt); the invite token is a server-side credential used to accept the invite and should be omitted (or redacted) from GET /api/orgs/{org}/members so it is never delivered to the client.

chronology.text: The user navigates to the members route of workspace qa-exploration-workspace (the frame shows the 'Loading route…' state); this triggers the client's fetch of the members endpoint (XGe in index-CPiqmCDG.js line 98640: fetch('/api/orgs/.../members')).

rootCause.text: The server-side members endpoint serializes the full invite record into the response, including the invite-acceptance credential: the response body of GET /api/orgs/qa-exploration-workspace/members contains `"invites":[{"token":"Tq7Xk2Vb9MwR4nLz8PcYd3HsGf6JaE1u",...}]`. The client never needs this value — MembersPage-BEGlMEYZ.js line 596 only references `s.token` as the React list key (children are rendered from `s.email`), and invite links are obtained separately from the POST /invites response's `link` field (index-CPiqmCDG.js line 98672 `f.link`). Since the field is present in the server's response to the browser and is not a legitimately client-facing token, the server is leaking the invite credential to the client.
